CRM.rationale: Salesforce presents a fundamentally strong but structurally complex picture. The core business is firing on all cylinders: Q1 FY2027 revenue of $11.13B grew +13.3% YoY, GAAP diluted EPS surged +52.2% YoY to $2.42, and operating cash flow hit $6.70B. The franchise is unmatched — #1 in CRM for 13 consecutive years with 20% market share, 150,000+ customers, and $67.9B total RPO providing deep revenue visibility. Agentforce has crossed $1.2B ARR (+205% YoY), signaling credible AI monetization. However, the balance sheet has deteriorated dramatically: total debt exploded to $39.28B while equity collapsed to $34.23B (D/E of 1.15x), driven by the massive $27.5B capital return program in Q1. This leverage materially reduces financial resilience. Valuation is attractive on a trailing P/E basis at 18.0x (vs. 365-day range of 16.3-57.4x) and even more so on a forward basis (~10.8x NTM per TIKR), well below peers like ServiceNow (~22.6x) and Microsoft (~20.1x). The Q2 guidance disappointment and slower growth vs. peers (13% vs. ServiceNow's 22%, HubSpot's 23%) temper enthusiasm. The Fin acquisition ($3.6B) adds execution risk but is strategically coherent for AI-powered customer service. On balance, the strong operating trajectory and depressed valuation offset the leverage concern enough to warrant a mildly positive score, but the balance sheet risk and growth deceleration prevent a stronger conviction.
